title: Krause et al., The complete mitochondrial DNA genome of an unknown hominin from southern Siberia
scope: Mitochondrial evidence from the fragment excavated in2008; the initial report is not the entire later nuclear-genome history.

title: Reich et al., Genetic history of an archaic hominin group from Denisova Cave in Siberia
scope: Nuclear comparisons, Neanderthal-related population history, another tooth and genetic contributions to later people; no recovered tribal name or exact journey.

title: Meyer et al., A high-coverage genome sequence from an archaic Denisovan individual
scope: Approximately30fold coverage; high coverage is not thirty sampled individuals or an entire population census.

title: Dabney, Meyer and Paabo, Ancient DNA damage
scope: Fragmentation and chemical changes; authentication uses multiple observations, not a visual glow or an infallible single stamp.

title: NHGRI, DNA Sequencing Fact Sheet
scope: Sequencing as reading the order of molecular bases; a sequence is not a recording of memories or ancient events.

title: NHGRI, Mitochondrial DNA glossary
scope: Separate mitochondrial genome, generally maternal inheritance; not the whole nuclear ancestry record.

title: NHGRI, Homologous Recombination glossary
scope: General recombination concept; teaching strips are not actual measured Denisovan sequences.

title: Douka et al., Age estimates for hominin fossils and the onset of the Upper Palaeolithic at Denisova Cave
scope: Fossil age models and ranges; distinguish discovery date, sample age, sediments and publication date. Do not reuse the oldest2010 age estimate as a settled exact age.

title: Jacobs et al., Timing of archaic hominin occupation of Denisova Cave in southern Siberia
scope: Stratigraphy and optical-dating framework; context and chronological uncertainty matter for attribution of activity.

title: Browning et al., Analysis of human sequence data reveals two pulses of archaic Denisovan admixture
scope: Evidence for complexity of contributions to later populations; no universal ancestry percentage or precise route.

title: Jacobs et al., Multiple deeply divergent Denisovan ancestries in Papuans
scope: Diverse Denisovan-related histories; one Altai reference is not all Denisovan populations everywhere.

title: Huerta-Sanchez et al., Altitude adaptation in Tibetans caused by introgression of Denisovan-like DNA
scope: EPAS1-region ancestry and high-altitude adaptation; not a whole-population ability determined by one gene and not a biography of the Altai individual.

title: Brown et al., Identification of a new hominin bone from Denisova Cave using collagen fingerprinting and mitochondrial DNA analysis
scope: ZooMS as screening for hominin material; screening alone must not be presented as final Denisovan identification.

title: Chen et al., A late Middle Pleistocene Denisovan mandible from the Tibetan Plateau
scope: Xiahe mandible, ancient proteins, minimum age approximately160ka from carbonate crust; not an exact death date or complete genome.

title: Zavala et al., Pleistocene sediment DNA reveals hominin and faunal turnovers at Denisova Cave
scope: Sediment mtDNA and changing representation of ancient groups; no exact personal identity from soil or assumed simultaneous occupation.

title: Zhang et al., Denisovan DNA in Late Pleistocene sediments from Baishiya Karst Cave on the Tibetan Plateau
scope: Independent sediment molecular evidence at Baishiya; remains distinct from the mandible protein study.

title: Xia et al., Middle and Late Pleistocene Denisovan subsistence at Baishiya Karst Cave
scope: Rib molecular identification and faunal/archaeological evidence; specimen photos are not copied into generated prompts.

title: Slon et al., The genome of the offspring of a Neanderthal mother and a Denisovan father
scope: Denisova11 first-generation parentage. Only abstract diagrams/objects: no portrait or youthful owner, no fictional meeting or family biography. This is a brief example; savedtopic7 is not produced here.

title: Tsutaya et al., A male Denisovan mandible from Pleistocene Taiwan
scope: Penghu1 molecular identification; alternative broad dating intervals and recovery history prohibit an invented exact age.

title: Fu et al., Denisovan mitochondrial DNA from dental calculus of the >146000-year-old Harbin cranium
scope: Mitochondrial evidence from dental calculus; minimum age146ka. Distinguish this from the protein study and from a complete universal portrait.

title: Fu et al., The proteome of the late Middle Pleistocene Harbin individual
scope: Protein evidence for Harbin Denisovan affinity; molecular affiliation does not settle all formal taxonomic naming.

title: Rao et al., Ancient proteins identify various Denisovan remains from Southwest China
scope: Bianfu identification of additional cranial/radial fragments and teeth; published before this document date, not an unverified future claim.

title: Denisovans from southwestern China and their subsistence strategies
scope: Companion Bianfu environment, fauna, tools and subsistence; association is not ownership by one identified individual.

title: The proteome of Middle Pleistocene Xujiayao and common Denisovan morphology
scope: Verified publisher/Crossmark online date21October2026. Protein-supported affiliation and broader comparisons; do not present every East Asian archaic fossil as definitively Denisovan.

title: Ethics of DNA research on human remains: five globally applicable guidelines
scope: Finite samples, documentation and stewardship; not an instruction to seek approval for this fictional/educational production.

title: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology, Denisovan Genome project
scope: Primary project overview linking2008 fragment and genome resources; not an additional independent confirmation of the same papers.

title: Orlando et al., Ancient DNA analysis
scope: General ancient-DNA methodological framework, contamination, analytical interpretation and limitations.
